candidates.statement: Under the process described in section 505G(c) of the FD&C Act, requestors can make minor 54 changes in the dosage form of an OTC monograph drug without the issuance of an order under 55 section 505G(b) of the FD&C Act 9 for the new dosage form if they maintain information 56 necessary to demonstrate that the change: (1) will not affect the safety or effectiveness of the 57 drug; and (2) will not materially affect the extent of absorption or other exposure to the active 58 ingredient(s) in comparison to a suitable reference product. 10 The change must also be in 59 conformity with the requirements of an applicable administrative order issued under section 60 505G(c)(3) of the FD&C Act. 11
candidates.context: On March 27, 2020, the President signed into law the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic 47 Security Act (CARES Act). In addition to its other measures, the CARES Act added section 48 505G to the FD&C Act. Section 505G reforms and modernizes the framework for the regulation 49 of OTC monograph drugs. 8 OTC monograph drugs may be marketed without an approved drug 50 application under section 505 of the FD&C Act if they meet the requirements of section 505G of 51 the FD&C Act, as well as other applicable requirements. 52 FDA is issuing proposed C001 under section 505G(c)(3) of the FD&C Act. This proposed order, 63 if finalized, will specify the requirements that must be met for a minor change in dosage form of 64 an OTC monograph drug from a capsule or tablet to a chewable tablet, ODT, or film. 65

candidates.statement: Solubility and permeability are active ingredient-specific characteristics; however, dissolution is 115 a product-specific characteristic, which may be impacted by product formulation or 116 manufacturing. Therefore, each time a requestor makes any formulation change or makes a 117 change in the manufacturing process related to the dosage form that is subject to C001 that could 118 impact the dissolution profile, the drug with that change or changes will need to meet the 119 requirements of C001, if finalized, for that dosage form to remain compliant with and 120 permissible under section 505G(c) of the FD&C Act. 121

candidates.statement: An active ingredient is classified as highly soluble if the highest single therapeutic dose is 125 completely soluble in 250 mL or less of aqueous media over the pH range of 1.2 to 6.8 at 126 37±1°C. The requestor should evaluate the solubility at equilibrium in at least three pH 127 conditions, including in buffers at pH 1.2, 4.5, and 6.8. 20 Buffers should be prepared as described 128 in the United States Pharmacopeia (USP), 21 and the pH should be verified (i.e., measured and 129 adjusted) after addition of the active ingredient and at the end of the solubility study to ensure the 130 solubility measurements are obtained under the specified pH. The requestor should conduct a 131 minimum of three replicate solubility determinations for each pH over a time frame suitable to 132 reach equilibrium using a shake-flask technique or an alternative method capable of adequately 133 predicting the equilibrium solubility of the active ingredient. Small volumes of solubility media 134 can be used if the available experimental apparatus will permit it. Alternatively, solubility 135 experiments where the highest therapeutic single dose is examined in a 250 mL volume, or a 136 proportionally smaller amount examined in a proportionally smaller volume of buffer, can be 137 used to demonstrate high solubility. 138

candidates.statement: Active ingredient permeability can be determined by either in vivo or in vitro methods. In vivo 150 permeability can be based on the extent of absorption derived from human pharmacokinetic 151 studies (e.g., absolute bioavailability or mass balance). High permeability can be concluded 152 when the absolute bioavailability is ≥85%. High permeability can also be concluded if ≥85% of 153 the administered dose is recovered in urine as unchanged (parent drug), or as the sum of parent 154 drug, Phase 1 oxidative and Phase 2 conjugative metabolites. Regarding metabolites in feces, 155 only oxidative and conjugative metabolites can be considered. Metabolites produced through 156 reduction or hydrolysis should not be included, unless the requestor maintains information to 157 demonstrate that they are not produced before absorption (e.g., by microbial action within the 158 gastrointestinal tract). As a scientific matter, unchanged drug in feces cannot be counted toward 159 the extent of absorption, unless appropriate data support that the amount of parent drug in feces 160 to be accounted for absorbed drug material is from biliary excretion or intestinal secretion or 161 originates from an unstable metabolite (e.g., glucuronide, sulfate, N-oxide) that has been 162 converted back to the parent by the action of microbial organisms. 163
candidates.context: Human in vivo data derived from published peer-reviewed literature (e.g., product knowledge 165 and bioavailability studies) can be appropriate; however, caution should be used when relying on 166 peer-reviewed literature as such literature might not contain the necessary details of the testing to 167 make a judgment regarding the quality of the results. 168

candidates.statement: 2 cells. Caco-2 epithelial cell monolayers derived from a human colon adenocarcinoma cell line 171 are widely used to estimate intestinal drug absorption in humans. Caco-2 cells undergo 172 spontaneous morphological and biochemical enterocytic differentiation and express cell polarity 173 with an apical brush border, tight intercellular junctions, and several active transporters as in the 174 small intestine. However, due to a potential for low or absent expression of efflux (e.g., P-gp, 175 BCRP, MRP2) and uptake (e.g., PepT1, OATP2B1, MCT1) transporters, the use of Caco-2 cell 176 assays as the sole data in support of high permeability classification is limited to passively 177 transported drugs. If high permeability is inferred by Caco-2 cell assays, the requestor should 178 demonstrate that permeability is independent of active transport. 179

candidates.statement: The requestor should justify the concentrations of the active ingredient used in the permeability 216 studies. A validated Caco-2 method used for drug permeability determinations should employ 217 conditions established during the validation and include a moderate and a high permeability 218 model drug in the donor fluid along with the active ingredient being tested as internal standards 219 to demonstrate consistency of the method. The requestor should choose internal standards based 220 on compatibility with the active ingredient (i.e., they should not exhibit any significant physical, 221 chemical, or permeation interactions). The permeability of the internal standards can be 222 determined following evaluation of the active ingredient in the same monolayers or monolayers 223 in the same plate when it is not feasible to include internal standards in the same cell culture well 224 as the active ingredient permeability evaluation. The permeability values of the internal 225 standards should be consistent between different tests, including those conducted during method 226 validation, and the requestor should set acceptance criteria for the internal standards and model 227 efflux drug. The requestor should assess mean drug and internal standards recovery at the end of 228 the test. For recoveries <80%, a mass balance evaluation should be conducted, including 229 measurement of the residual amount of drug in the cell monolayer and testing apparatus. 230

candidates.statement: Chewable tablets are intended to be chewed or crushed and then swallowed by the consumer 319 rather than swallowed whole. Critical quality attributes for chewable tablets include, but are not 320 limited to, hardness, disintegration, and dissolution. Additional considerations such as tablet size 321 and taste can affect the ability or willingness of a consumer to chew the chewable tablet. Product 322 attributes should ensure the performance of the chewable tablet for its intended use. See the 323 guidance for industry Quality Attribute Considerations for Chewable Tablets (August 2018) for 324 recommendations on critical quality attributes that should be assessed for chewable tablets. 325

candidates.statement: Films for oral administration are intended to rapidly disintegrate on the tongue and incorporate 337 the active ingredient into saliva before being swallowed. Palatability, film dimensions, film 338 integrity, and disintegration are critical quality attributes for this dosage form. Film dimensions 339 should be appropriate for the oral route of administration and the intended consumer population. 340 In addition, the film should be substantial enough to maintain its integrity during manufacturing 341 and permit handling by the consumer. 342

candidates.statement: Under section 505G(c) of the FD&C Act, a requestor must maintain information necessary to 347 demonstrate that the minor change in dosage form will not affect the safety or effectiveness of 348 the drug. In § C001.60(a)(1)(B) of C001, the Agency proposes that requestors must maintain 349 information demonstrating that the packaging of 505G(c) products is consistent with the 350 requirements described in Proposed Administrative Order OTC000037 titled Over-the-Counter 351 Monograph Condition B001: Single-Unit or Unit-Dose Containers for Over-the-Counter 352 Monograph Drugs in Orally Disintegrating Tablet and Film Dosage Forms (hereinafter referred 353 to as B001), if finalized. 37 This information is necessary to demonstrate that the change in 354 dosage form will not materially affect the extent of absorption or other exposure to the active 355 ingredient in comparison to the suitable reference product or affect the safety or effectiveness of 356 the drug. If B001 is finalized, OTC monograph drugs in an ODT or film dosage form that are 357 subject to an OTC monograph identified in B001 must be packaged in single-unit or unit-dose 358 containers as a condition for being considered generally recognized as safe and effective and not 359 misbranded. 360

PACKAGING AND RECORDKEEPING 345 In B001 FDA proposes that certain OTC monograph drugs in an ODT or film dosage form must 362 be in single-unit or unit-dose containers to address potential safety and efficacy concerns posed, 363 in part, because these dosage forms dissolve quickly in the mouth and are designed to be more 364 palatable than other oral dosage forms such as tablets and capsules. The palatability and rapid 365 dissolution of ODTs and films make them more attractive to and can pose greater risks of 366 accidental ingestion by young children. Moreover, ODTs can break apart when handled or stored 367 in high humidity, which could result in underdosing from a multiple-unit container. Films 368 packaged in multiple-unit containers have the potential to stick together, making it easy for a 369 consumer to inadvertently dose more than one film at the same time. 370
